html:
John III Sobieski was king of Poland and grand duke of Lithuania from 1674 to 1696, born in 1629 in Olesko castle near Lviv, today in Ukraine, best known for leading the army that broke the siege of Vienna in 1683.

A noble general, he made his name fighting the Ottomans and won a great victory at Khotyn in 1673, after which he was elected king. On 12 September 1683 he led the largest cavalry charge in history, with the winged hussars, against the Ottoman army camped before Vienna and routed it. He reported to the Pope that they came, they saw, and God conquered. The victory began the Ottoman retreat from central Europe. At home he could not strengthen royal power, and the Commonwealth kept declining. His palace at Wilanów in Warsaw survives.
